steps.title: Open the Cockpit
steps.narration: Tapeology opens on the Cockpit — a live, simulated, or historical trading-tape viewer, with no sign-in needed.
steps.point_out: The page loads idle, hinting to try a ticker like SIM-BUYER, with a top navigation bar showing just two links.

steps.title: Type a ticker to watch
steps.narration: Typing a simulated ticker into the ticker field is the first step to watching a live tape settle.
steps.point_out: "SIM-BUYER" now sits in the ticker field, ready to watch.

steps.title: Watch it settle to a market read
steps.narration: Clicking Watch starts the simulated tape; within a few seconds it reads which side is in control of the price action.
steps.point_out: The Tape State panel now reads "Buyer Control", and a live candlestick price chart has appeared above it.

steps.title: Switch the chart's bar size
steps.narration: The live price chart can be re-grouped into wider logical bars on the fly, without losing the live feed.
steps.point_out: "30s" is now highlighted, the caption updates, and the chart redraws with fewer, wider candles built live from the tape.

expect.text: Logical 30s bars built live from the tape.

steps.title: Stop the watch
steps.narration: Stopping instantly clears the tape back to its idle state — the watch-and-stop loop still works end to end.
steps.point_out: The page returns to "No ticker watched".

steps.title: Move to the Structure page
steps.narration: The top navigation shows exactly two links — Cockpit and Structure — nothing left over from the research pages retired this chapter.
steps.point_out: The Structure page's framing paragraph now mentions Case Studies again — a sentence that had gone missing and is reinstated this iteration.

expect.text: Case Studies lists every band-touch event

steps.title: Enter a symbol to study
steps.narration: Loading Structure starts with a symbol and a point in time.
steps.point_out: "AAPL" now sits in the Symbol field.

steps.title: Enter the as-of date
steps.narration: The as-of field pins the exact moment the levels and chart are computed for.
steps.point_out: The as-of field now reads the chosen date and time.

steps.title: Load AAPL's tradable map
steps.narration: Loading a symbol and a date renders its candlestick chart together with a shaded support/resistance wall band.
steps.point_out: The chart shows AAPL's candles with a tradable wall band around 300.11 to 302.2, and a table below it lists that band's details.

steps.title: Browse every recorded price-wall touch
steps.narration: Scrolling down reveals the Case Studies panel — a list of every recorded support/resistance band touch — which had been hidden from the page until this chapter's clean-up restored it. Typing a symbol narrows the list instantly.
steps.point_out: The table narrows to AAPL's recorded events only, each row showing its band, its reaction, and its forward returns.

steps.title: Open a case-study drill-in
steps.narration: Clicking any row opens a detailed drill-in for that specific event.
steps.point_out: The drill-in repeats the row's band and reaction, then shows either a recorded tape timeline or the honest note that no tape was recorded for that event.

steps.title: Check the Edge Report's honest state
steps.narration: The Edge Report compares three trading strategies over recorded windows — when it has not been computed yet, it says so plainly instead of showing a blank panel, and offers a button to start the comparison.
steps.point_out: Clicking Compute edge report immediately switches the label to "Computing…" and shows a live progress line, confirming the control is wired up.

steps.title: Cancel the compute run
steps.narration: Cancelling stops the run cleanly and leaves no long job running in the background.
steps.point_out: The Cancel button confirms it is finishing the current backtest before stopping.

steps.title: Confirm a retired page is really gone
steps.narration: Visiting one of the three removed research pages directly still shows the app's plain not-found screen, never a stale leftover page.
steps.point_out: "This page could not be found" appears, and the same two-item navigation bar is still there at the top.

expect.text: This page could not be found.

steps.title: Back to the Cockpit
steps.narration: Clicking back through the trimmed navigation confirms both pages still connect correctly.
steps.point_out: The nav bar shows only "Cockpit" and "Structure" — nothing left over from the three retired pages — and the Cockpit is back to its idle state.
